# RTL numeric font context

Original OOXML generated by `tools/rtl_font_context_fixture.py`, using only the
OPC skeleton of our original rtl-runs control. Fifty-one cases span eight pages.
Ordinary formatting is Arial 10pt (hAnsi Times New Roman); complex-script
formatting is Courier New bold 16pt. The controls vary surrounding scripts,
numeric punctuation, ASCII/Persian/Arabic-Indic digits, tabs, split color runs,
cs-only and combined cs/rtl declarations. No corpus content is copied.

The reference application produced `native.pdf` through `tools/export-reference.ps1`.
`tools/record_rtl_font_context_reference.py` records every glyph's font, size,
weight and origin, and binds the original source/PDF/case hashes.

## Reference/spec divergence

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.2.30 requires the cs/cstheme face for rtl text. The published MS-OI29500
[rFonts note](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/aef3c9a6-5d6c-434b-90b7-85e761fd8e62)
also describes unconditional cs-face selection. Case 1 is a counterexample using
only weak numeric characters: the reference application chooses Arial Bold 16pt for `012` despite
the explicit Courier New cs declaration. Size and bold still come from szCs/bCs.
Case 39 repeats that behavior with both cs and rtl; cs-only case 19 uses Courier.
These cases do not rely on the specification-unspecified combination of strong
LTR letters with rtl=true. Latin-containing controls separately record native
compatibility for that unspecified combination.

The observed rule selects the ordinary ASCII face for ASCII numeric groups in
RTL context. A preceding Latin strong character retains the cs face; Hebrew or
Arabic context uses the numeric exception. The context survives equivalent run
splits but resets after tabs. Separators between numbers and adjacent terminators
belong to the numeric group; a group containing non-ASCII characters keeps cs.
This explains different behavior for `$12` and `£12` without font-name or
document-specific exceptions. A slash is a directional separator rather than
part of the numeric group in the reference application's RTL handling. A leading plus/minus is also
separate, whereas an internal plus between digits belongs to the group.

The implementation uses Unicode bidi classes to identify groups, preserving
source text and declarations. It is a native compatibility rule, not a claim
that Unicode W2/W7 prescribes font selection. The source declarations never
change, including ordinary and complex-script size/bold values.

## Verification and limits

Unit tests compare every non-whitespace glyph's font and weight with the native
reference and check source-model preservation. The reference application's PDF maps Persian zero to
the same Courier glyph as Arabic zero; only the test oracle normalizes that
ToUnicode alias. The engine preserves the original code point.

The browser test now imports the original control DOCX through
openCanvasDocument and uses the real read-only CanvasEditor, including
color-window painting. All eight rasters match the previously checked
equivalent internal-paragraph model exactly. All eight native/app
page pairs were inspected. Page/line counts, body baselines, suffix positions,
resolved RTL visual order and split-run blue ink are checked. Maximum measured
suffix-origin difference is .152pt; baseline difference is .070pt. These are
component controls. Strict active RTL/cs editing is still guarded; read-only
import retains these declarations.
Default/missing CS faces, italic missing-glyph fallback, full explicit Unicode
control semantics and editing run-boundary/keyboard behavior remain open.


Native browser comparisons require locally installed Arial, Courier New and
Times New Roman faces; CSS aliases do not establish native-font availability.
They skip with an explicit reason when those prerequisites are absent, without
loosening native tolerances. The separate bundled-family bidi browser control
continues checking ordering, caret hit testing and source preservation on hosts
without those native faces. A skipped comparison is not native fidelity proof.
